senses: a pageant (usu. in a cycle of mystery plays, esp. as performed by guild of craftsmen)
la:noun:pagina.html:
pāgĭna, ae, f.
root pag-(pak-), of pango, πήγνυμι; v. pagus
,
a written page or leaf: paginae dictae, quod ... in illis versus panguntur, id est figuntur, Müll.
Lit.: cum hanc paginam tenerem,: complere paginam,: tantas paginas commovere,; : censoriarum legum paginae,: millesima pagina,.— Prov.: fortuna paginam utramque facit, fills both sides of the account, confers both good and ill fortune (alluding to accountbooks, in which the receipts were written on one page and the expenses on the opposite one), .—
Transf.
A page, for any writing, a letter, book, etc.: varie sum affectus tuis litteris: valde priore paginā perturbatus, paulum alterā recreatus,: respondi postremae tuae paginae,: lasciva est nobis pagina, vita proba,: profana,.—
A leaf, slab: vel tabellas qualescumque marmoreas aut paginas imprimemus,: insignis honorum,a plate on which are engraved a person's titles and honors,.—
In vine-dressers' lang., four rows of vines joined together in a square, a bed or quarter, .

la:adj:paganus.gloss: of or pertaining to the countryside, rural, rustic
senses: of or pertaining to the countryside, rural, rustic
la:adj:paganus.html:
pāgānus, a, um, adj.
pagus
.
Of or belonging to the country or to a village, rustic: PORTICVS, Inscr. (A. U. C. 659) Orell. 3793: lex,: foci,.—
Subst.: pāgānus, i, m., a countryman, peasant, villager, rustic: nulli pagani aut montani,: pagani vel decuriones, Cod. Th. 7, 21, 2.—
Opposed to military, civil, civic: vel paganum est peculium vel castrense,.—As subst.: pāgānus, i, m., a civilian, a citizen, : paganorum turba,: milites et pagani,; .—
Transf., rustic, unlearned: cultus,; cf. semipaganus.—
In eccl. Lat. (like gentilis) for heathen, pagan (opp. Jewish or Christian); and subst., a heathen, a pagan: ritus cultusque, Cod. Th. 16, 7, 2: sacerdotales paganae superstitionis,; : deorum falsorum multorumque cultores paganos vocamus,; : ex locorum agrestium compitis et pagis pagani vocantur,

la:noun:pagus.html:
pāgus, i (old
gen. PAGEIEI, which prob. is an error for PAGEI, ), m.
root pak-, pag-, to make fast or firm, whence pango, pax, pagina; Gr. πήγνυμι, πάγος, etc.; prop., a place with fixed boundaries; hence
, a district, canton, province (opp. to the city), the country (cf. vicus): paganalia (feriae sunt eorum) qui sunt aliquoius pagi,; cf. § 26 Müll.: Lemonia tribus a pago Lemonio appellata est, Paul. ex : pagos et compita circum,: omissis pagis vicisque,: MAGISTER PAGI,a country magistrate,: si me toto laudet vicinia pago,.—Of the districts, cantons, of the Gauls and Germans: in Galliā ... in omnibus pagis partibusque,; ; ; 22; 6, 23; 7, 64; : cum Alamannorum pagos aliquos esse reputaret hostiles,.—
Transf.
The country people: festus in pratis vacat otioso Cum bove pagus,: pagus agat festum,.—
Novem Pagi, a city in Belgic Gaul, now Dieuze, (al. Decem Pagi).
